summary: Phase 149O.19.3R.1 -- HMIC Frozen Implementation Identity Contract Repair Independent Re-Verification: independent-re-verification-only phase (no src/pcae/** file modified; no contract file modified). Confirmed baseline via direct inspection: repo clean at entry, origin/main..HEAD=0, 149O.19.3R completed/complete at 942df2a2, HMIC-001 status FROZEN -- REPAIRED, PENDING INDEPENDENT RE-VERIFICATION, hardcoded False ceiling unchanged, HATP production NOT READY, runtime Observed/observe/unavailable. Without trusting 149O.19.3R's own dependency table, read the repaired HMIC-001 contract and all 22 currently-frozen production files directly, and independently re-walked PCAE-owned transitive imports from all 22 files (AST-based, fresh from source). Independently reimplemented implementation_scope_digest from the contract's normative text (not reusing 149O.19.3R's helper) and confirmed it is deterministic and sensitive to a byte mutation in each of the four newly-added files. Reproduced the original pre-repair defect (mutations to hatp_providers.py/hatp_fido2_provider.py/hatp_piv_provider.py/hatp_hardware_credentials.py do not change the digest under the historical 18-file model) and confirmed the repair closes it (the same mutations do change the digest under the current 22-file model). Confirmed all four newly-frozen files BOUND: hatp_providers.py (provider registration/lookup/selection/dispatch), hatp_fido2_provider.py (FIDO2 assertion accept/reject), hatp_piv_provider.py (PIV verification, structurally classified authority-sensitive despite being deferred/non-operational), hatp_hardware_credentials.py (public-key material FIDO2 signatures are checked against). Re-examined hatp_bootstrap.py, repository_identity.py, permission_broker.py, permission_broker_foundation.py, the AG3/AG5 effect-gate owner, hatp_mandatory_cutover.py, RAE/PB/effect-gate authority code, and human-approval/rollback-evidence verifiers -- each confirmed either inside the 22-file set or correctly excluded with documented rationale. Transitive closure verdict: YES -- the 22-file set is sufficient; no further class-A authority-sensitive file found unbound. Found one non-Blocking documentation gap: hatp_signing_ceremony.py is dynamically imported (importlib.import_module) inside hatp_mandatory_cutover.py's readiness assessment but is not discussed in 149O.19.3R's own dependency table; independently confirmed its exclusion is correct on the merits (import-existence probe only, output re-verified by the frozen chain, zero trust credit) -- a documentation-completeness gap, not a binding defect. Future-HMIC-validator self-reference question re-examined: NON-BLOCKING CONCERN, explicitly and non-silently deferred by the contract to a future phase; no validator code exists yet to bind. Editable-install/PYTHONPATH-shadow concerns re-assessed consistent with 149O.19.3's prior disposition. Re-extracted requirement/invariant/attack-matrix counts fresh from contract text: 144 sequential HMIC-REQ IDs (gap-free), 12 CIVC invariants, attack matrix re-confirmed. Added a new 29-test independent re-verification module (tests/test_phase_149o_19_3r_1_hmic_frozen_identity_repair_independent_reverification.py) with independently-derived expectations (not copied from 149O.19.3R's own test constants): transitive-walk structural checks, digest sensitivity across the 22-file set, and the historical-18-vs-current-22 mutation comparison. Regression run (149O.19.2 freeze + 149O.19.3 verification + 149O.19.3R repair suites, combined): 103 passed, 0 failed. New suite: 29 passed, 0 failed. Fast Green under the repository's pinned interpreter (.venv/bin/python3, CPython 3.9.6): 28 failed/5563 passed/1 skipped before this phase's new test file existed, 28 failed/5592 passed/1 skipped after -- the identical 28 named pre-existing/unrelated failures in both runs (older 149O.16/149O.17/149O.18*-phase byte-diff/file-allowlist tests anchored to their own historical baselines, none referencing HMIC-001 or the four newly-frozen files), passed count increased by exactly 29 matching this phase's new suite, zero new failures. Broad -k "hmic or 149o_19_3 or hatp" sweep: 133 failed/2728 passed/3 skipped; confirmed via git stash -u A/B (this phase's changes fully removed) that the identical 133 failures (same names) and exactly 29 fewer passes (2699) appear in the baseline, confirming all 133 are pre-existing and unrelated. Verdicts: B-149O.19.3-1 INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED CLOSED (qualifier: frozen implementation identity transitive under-binding repaired). HMIC verification verdict: VERIFIED WITH NON-BLOCKING FINDINGS -- HMIC-001 v1.0 CONFORMS. Implementation identity verdict: (B) safe with non-blocking limitations. Provider-layer verdict: all four newly-frozen files BOUND. Transitive closure verdict: YES. Validator self-reference verdict: NON-BLOCKING CONCERN. Recommended next phase: 149O.19.4 (implementation-plan-only) may proceed; an optional documentation-only follow-up may add an explicit contract-repair-history table row for hatp_signing_ceremony.py at the team's discretion (not a blocking prerequisite). No certification artifact, active-certification pointer, or revocation record created anywhere in the repository. No Cutover Record or activation marker created or modified. No real Class-B provisioning. No real HATP_MANDATORY activation occurred anywhere. B-149O-1..4 verdict unchanged, carried forward: INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED CLOSED AT SYSTEM IMPLEMENTATION/ENFORCEMENT BOUNDARY -- DEPLOYMENT/OPERATIONAL ACTIVATION DEFERRED. HATP production remains NOT READY. Runtime remains Observed / observe / unavailable.
